newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rates stable, demand slackens.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rates stable, demand slackens.

text.p: Croatian money rates were mostly stable on Wednesday amid abundant supply of kuna while interbank demand slackened, dealers said.
"Lenders showered us this morning with their surplus money but to their disappointment demand remained low," dealer Jasenka Blagaic said.
Fresh money deals totalled a meagre 8.7 million kuna by 0900 GMT, leaving an extra 70 million on offer.
But banks increased Lombard loans from the central bank to 96 million kuna from 40.5 million at the end of Monday.
Call money loans were made at a stable seven percent rate.
One smaller one-month deal was struck at 13.5 percent, 50 basis points higher than Tuesday, while 90-day money was granted at a steady 18 percent.
Banks had 583 million kuna on their accounts on Tuesday and none had any shortfalls. Only one bank borrowed 10 million kuna in overnight trade to maintain its reserve requirement.
Banking liquidity is expected to receive a further boost after a central bank purchase of hard currency due later today, dealers said. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
